At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.
 As a Data Scientist on the Mapping team, you will collaborate with our world class team of scientists, engineers, product managers, and designers to grow and improve the quality of recommended routes and accuracy of our travel time estimations. We're looking for a passionate, driven Data Scientist who is excited to dive into our geospatial, behavioural and mobility data, and build a best-in-class mapping product that provides safe, efficient, and seamless navigation for our rideshare drivers.
 Data Science is at the heart of Lyft’s products and decision-making. You will leverage data and rigorous, analytical thinking to shape our mapping products and make business decisions that put our customers first. The Mapping team serves models and systems that determine the most efficient routes, fastest travel estimates and process real-time map data signals to detect traffic, closures and slowdowns. Working with our business and analytics partners, the team owns tools to ensure Lyft offers routes that our users trust. This will involve identifying and scoping opportunities, recommending technical solutions, designing experiments, and measuring the impact of new features. You will help us solve some of the most impactful problems in Mapping, including:
 How do we accurately predict acute and chronic traffic conditions?
 How do we improve the recommendations of our routing algorithms?
 How do we keep our travel estimation promises to our riders and drivers?
 How do we benchmark and measure the success of our services?

 Own the complete lifecycle of algorithmic solutions from problem formulation, data exploration, and feature engineering to deployment, monitoring, and iteration
 Prioritize and lead deep dives into our data to uncover new product and business opportunities
 Partner closely with Engineering to build and scale production-grade ML systems, real-time inference services, batch pipelines, and feature stores
 Design, implement, and analyze different types of experiments, and facilitate and foster data-driven and informed decision making and prioritization
 Drive scientific excellence by introducing modern techniques in ML, optimization, reinforcement learning, or graph-based methods to unlock new product capabilities
 Establish metrics that measure the health of our products, as well as rider and driver experience
 Translate complex business challenges into concrete algorithmic solutions in close collaboration with Product, Engineering, Operations, and Science teams
 Experience:
 Advanced degree in a quantitative field such as statistics, physics, economics, operations research, neuroscience, or engineering, or relevant work experience
 3+ years hands-on experience in a data science or machine learning role working with production machine learning models and optimization systems
 Passion for solving unstructured and non-standard mathematical problems
 Experience independently driving multi-project algorithmic scopes and navigating technical ambiguity from ideation to delivery
 Experience with machine learning models in production, making practical tradeoffs among algorithm sophistication, compute complexity, maintainability, and extensibility in production environments
 Strong oral and written communication skills, and ability to collaborate with and influence cross-functional partners 
 Working knowledge of modern machine learning frameworks and distributed computing systems, including PyTorch, TensorFlow, Ray, Spark, etc.

Job Title: Power System Engineering Technologist (P.L. Eng.)
 Job Level: ENG C
 Date Posted: September 8, 2026
 Closing Date: Open until the positions is filled
 Job Type: Full-time Permanent
 Category: Internal/External Opportunities 
 Location: Calgary
 Powering a bright future starts with you! 
 At AltaLink, people are at the heart of our success. We are a team committed to doing the right thing for each other and our customers. We foster an environment that is inclusive, collaborative and high performing and we value personal accountability. Our people are empowered to continuously improve, deliver outstanding customer service and make a meaningful impact every day. We embrace the unique identities, experiences and perspectives of our workforce, reflecting the communities where we operate. Everyone at AltaLink can expect to work in a safe, respectful environment where trust and commitment are at the core of how we operate. 
 Oh, and, what do we do? 
 We power Alberta! Our transmission lines deliver electricity to millions of Albertans 24 hours a day, seven days a week. When you’re on our team, you’re supporting Alberta’s homes, farms, businesses and industries by providing the safe, reliable and affordable electricity they rely on. Whether working in the field or in the office, every AltaLinker contributes to keeping the lights on. Want to join our team? We’re excited to share that we are hiring a Power System Engineering Technologist (P.L.Eng.) on AltaLink’s Project Engineering team.
 Job Description: 
 AltaLink is seeking a Power System Engineering Technologist (P.L. Eng.) to join the Project Engineering team. The successful candidate will focus on development, validation, and management of transmission-system and electrical-equipment models. They will work with internal teams, the AESO, and other stakeholders, to prepare transmission modelling data packages (PDUPs), line-impedance calculations, and facility-rating reports; support small interconnection studies; provide system-capacity, power-flow, and short-circuit information; and help improve modelling processes and procedures. The role is also responsible for ensuring modelling data records, documentation, and submissions comply with applicable AESO ISO Rules, Alberta Reliability Standards, and associated requirements. 
 This opportunity is open to individuals who are registered with the Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of Alberta (APEGA) as a Professional Licensee (Engineering), P.L. (Eng.), or individuals who are eligible to obtain that designation. The successful candidate will apply sound technical judgement, maintain accurate and auditable modelling records, and contribute to the safe, reliable, and economic interconnection to and operation of Alberta’s transmission system.
 Responsibilities: 
 Under the supervision of the Manager, Project Engineering, this individual will be accountable for all or in part of the following: 
 Development, authentication, and submission of complete, accurate, and timely transmission modelling data packages to the AESO for existing facilities and planned additions, modifications, and re-ratings of electrical facilities and infrastructure in accordance with AESO modelling-data requirements.
 Validation and maintenance of existing transmission-system and electrical-equipment models to ensure they accurately represent current facility configurations, equipment characteristics, operating conditions, and approved system changes.
 Development and maintenance of line-impedance calculations and reports.
 Development and maintenance of facility-rating reports for existing and planned transmission facilities.
 Ensuring modelling data, models, supporting documentation, and submissions comply with applicable AESO ISO Rules, Alberta Reliability Standards, and AltaLink Standards.
 Supporting the delivery of facility studies for system and customer projects, by providing transmission modelling, current and future system capacity assessments, power flow analysis, and short circuit information to other internal teams and external customers.
 Collaborating with AESO teams to improve modelling processes and procedures.
 Demonstrate key behaviors and meet identified expectations outlined in our four cultural pillars – one team, continuous improvement, customer focus and personal accountability.
 Qualifications: 
 Electrical Engineering Technology Diploma. A focus on power systems is considered an asset.
 Professional Licensee (Engineering) P.L. Eng designation with the Association of Professional Engineers & Geoscientists of Alberta (APEGA) or eligible to obtain such designation, with a defined scope of practice applicable to the duties of the position.
 Minimum of six 6 years of relevant experience related to engineering or modeling of high voltage transmission or distributions systems. Preference will be given to candidates with two or more years of specific engineering experience related to the modeling of electrical transmission and/or distribution systems and to candidates with a working knowledge of AESO rules and requirements. 
 Proven ability/experience in the above noted responsibilities.
 Technical knowledge and understanding of transmission system modeling operation and planning.
 Documented experience with PTI’s (Power Technology Incorporated) PSSE program and other power system analysis tools such as PSCAD/EMTDC is an asset.
 Familiar with the AESO Modeling Data requirements and rules.
 Strong verbal and written (reporting, graphical) communication skills with ability to work in a team environment and positively influence others.
 Effective communication and interpersonal skills to interface with team members and customers to promote positive customer outcomes.
 Excellent organizational skills and ability to manage a wide variety of issues on multiple projects simultaneously.  
 Working knowledge of Microsoft Office: Word, Power Point, Excel etc.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers, while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be. The way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011, but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ahVf4AjYlh4.

 

The Team:

The Enablement team is a central function within Jobber’s Customer Success organization, supporting the growth and performance of Product Support and Customer Onboarding. As a Center of Excellence, Enablement owns the programs, playbooks, tools, and measurement frameworks that drive operational excellence and skill development across these teams. We work cross-functionally to ensure that every team member, regardless of channel or customer type, has the knowledge, confidence, and support to deliver value. That value is measured in outcomes: customers who activate faster, stay longer, and get more out of the product.

The Role:

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Success Enablement, the Success Enablement Manager will give our Product Support and Customer Onboarding teams the information, content, and tools they need to operate more effectively.

You will own enablement end to end for both teams. That means building how specialists ramp, how they stay current as the product changes, how they access the right answer in the moment, and how they keep improving once they are proficient. It also means raising the ceiling on what those conversations deliver. An onboarding session that activates a business on the features it actually needs, and a high-quality support interaction that also surfaces a product or feature the customer is missing, are both revenue moments. Service quality comes first in both. A specialist who has not solved the problem in front of them has not earned the next conversation. Your job is to make that judgement teachable, repeatable, and measurable.

You will build the needs discovery and product positioning frameworks specialists use live, enable the Next Best Action recommendations that surface in their workspace, and partner closely with our frontline manager group to help them hit their KPIs across service levels, quality, activation, adoption, and retention.

The Success Enablement Manager will:

 - Own the enablement lifecycle for Product Support and Customer Onboarding, from new hire ramp and certification through continuous development for tenured specialists.

 - Build and maintain the needs discovery and positioning frameworks specialists use in live customer conversations, so the right product reaches the right customer at the right moment.

 - Create and maintain Jobber’s Support and Onboarding playbooks, including activation paths by plan and industry, adoption plays for underused features, objection handling, and retention conversations, and ensure consistency of process and messaging across channels.

 - Enable Next Best Action adoption. Train specialists to read the recommendation, confirm the customer need behind it, and act on it inside their existing workflow.

 - Design, build and test in-person, virtual and on-demand enablement content, and partner with Knowledge Management so the same guidance is available in the flow of work.

 - Partner with our QA function to turn quality trends into targeted coaching and training, closing the loop between what we measure and what we teach.

 - Work with Product Marketing, Success Operations and Analytics to identify process and content gaps, and develop the resources (customer stories, competitive intelligence, collateral) that help specialists move conversations forward.

 - Connect enablement to outcomes. Tie program delivery to activation, feature adoption, retention, CSAT, and qualified opportunities, and report on what is working and what is not.

 - Contribute to, help organize and champion important team moments like quarterly kickoffs, lunch and learns, and certification pushes.

To be successful, you should have:

 - Demonstrated experience in customer success, customer service, onboarding, or sales within a high volume, short cycle, B2B SaaS environment, with a track record of consistent achievement of targets and motivating others to do the same.

 - Demonstrated previous experience in revenue driven roles which had targets, such as in Sales or Retention.

 - Experience building out and executing playbooks and training programs that improve both service quality and commercial outcomes.

 - Strong project management knowledge, including creating workback plans to drive projects from conception to the finish line.

 - A strong grasp of activation and adoption. You understand what gets a customer to first value, what keeps them using a product, and how to design enablement that moves both.

 - Working knowledge of needs-based conversations. You can teach a specialist to uncover a customer problem, connect it to the right product or feature, and position the value in plain language.

 - A knack for identifying gaps in our process and how to fill them. Thinking beyond our current process and coming up with smart solutions.

 - A high level of organizational and time management skills.

 - The ability to collaborate with business partners across the organization. Working with specialists, Product Marketing and other leadership members, you’ll be required to articulate strategic ideas, learn the inner workings of Jobber, and then deliver on high-level concepts.

 - The ability to teach yourself, and others. Our team uses a variety of tools, so you’ll need to learn the most efficient uses of them and then spread that knowledge amongst the team.

 Job Description: 
 Primary Purpose  
 The Specialist, New Student Transition (Graduate), is responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining integrated programs intended to support a successful transition for new and incoming graduate students into the university. This requires the Specialist to be knowledgeable and up to date on the unique needs of graduate students with special attention and focus on international students and priority populations (e.g., Black, Indigenous, racialized, 2SLGBTQIA+ and historically underrepresented groups). The Specialist will work collaboratively and strategically with key internal and external stakeholders and is responsible for overseeing the implementation of graduate transition programs including day to day operations, decision making and program leadership. The Specialist will work closely with the Manager, New Student Transition and New Student Transition (NST) team to ensure programs are well integrated, responsive to the needs of the faculties and campus partners and are achieving desired outcomes.  The Specialist may also contribute to the coordination and administration of NST-wide initiatives, processes, and projects, as appropriate. The Specialist demonstrates a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion and anti-racism through their leadership, program design and operational practices. 
 The Specialist has three primary areas of focus: 1) Design, implement, assess and maintain graduate student transition programming; ensure initiatives are well-integrated and coordinated into the overall new student transition strategy and contribute to the coordination of NST-wide initiatives and processes as appropriate, 2) Be knowledgeable and up to date on the needs of incoming graduate students, including priority populations (e.g., Black, Indigenous, racialized, 2SLGBTQIA+, historically underrepresented groups and international graduate students) and 3) Maintain positive working relationships with key campus and faculty partners and graduate students.
 Key Accountabilities   
 Program Development and Administration 
 Develops, coordinates, and maintains targeted programs and initiatives designed to ensure the successful transition of new graduate students for all three academic terms via virtual, in-person or hybrid offerings.
 Apply research, best practices, and knowledge of student trends to develop and execute specialized programming for priority graduate student populations, including priority populations (e.g., Black, Indigenous, racialized, 2SLGBTQIA+ and historically underrepresented groups) and international graduate students. 
 Leverages resources, knowledge, and expertise in the SSO to assist in the design of transition programs when appropriate in partnership with the SSO leadership team and campus partners.
 With the Manager, New Student Transition and SSO leadership team, identifies and develops additional supports/initiatives for graduate students throughout their academic career beyond existing transition programming.
 ·       Provides guidance to stakeholders on campus who support new student transition programs/opportunities to create an engaged and inclusive community of University of Waterloo graduate students. 
 ·       Contributes to the overall graduating student experience by assisting UWaterloo’s convocation team to support fall and spring convocation ceremonies.
 ·       Applies an equity, diversity, inclusion, and anti-racism lens to all program design elements.
 Relationship Building  
 Works closely with both the NST team and International Experience Centre (IEC) to ensure programs and strategies complement one another and, when appropriate, are consistent in delivery and outcomes for all incoming students.
 Collaborates with campus partners to ensure students are provided with necessary support, resources, and information pertinent to their University of Waterloo experience. Key campus partners include but are not limited to: International Experience Centre, Graduate Student Association, Graduate Studies and Postdoctoral Affairs, Campus Housing, Campus Wellness, AccessAbility Services, Community Relations, and all Faculties and affiliated University Colleges as applicable.
 Facilitates strong working relationships with SSO colleagues, particularly the NST  team, and collaborates on strategies that will support the successful transition of new undergraduate and graduate students and contribute to an overall positive student experience across multiple portfolios within the SSO.  
 Establishes and maintains a network of relationships with external organizations (e.g.: Canadian Association for Graduate Studies, etc.) to remain up to date on new research, strategies and initiatives in orientation programs and new student transition literature. 
 Participates in and contributes to regular staff, department, and Faculty specific meetings as appropriate.
 Staff and Volunteer Development   
 Provides strong leadership to student staff including setting clear and reasonable goals and expectations, providing on-going feedback, and establishing a strong foundation for performance through comprehensive training and on-going professional development as required.
 Outlines clear expectations and responsibilities for student staff and volunteers, as they relate to graduate student transition programming. 
 Responsible for the recruitment, hiring, selection, ongoing training, appreciation, and recognition of student staff, including co-op students.  Works closely with staff in the SSO and IEC , to ensure compensation and appreciation of student staff and volunteers is equitable. 
 Maintains consistent and appropriate levels of communication with student-staff and volunteers to ensure ongoing engagement and accountability. 
 Provides support to UWaterloo’s convocation team to recruit, train, and schedule a small team of campus volunteers for each ceremony as needed.
 Research and reporting 
 Strong understanding of the graduate student experience at the University of Waterloo, particularly priority populations (e.g., Black, Indigenous, racialized, 2SLGBTQIA+ and historically underrepresented groups) and international students.
 Applies current research, best practices, student development theory, and student trends to design intentional, proactive, and responsive orientation programs that are in line with the needs of our students and Faculty partners.
 With the NST Manager, the Specialist contributes to the strategic priorities of their portfolio, providing regular progress reports and updates to internal and external partners.
 Works closely with the NST Manager to summarize and disseminate key research related to new student transition programming.  
 Connects as needed with the IEC team to share information related to the new student experience for international graduate students.
 Required Qualifications    
   Education 
 University degree required; Master’s degree or equivalent experience in a related field (e.g., Leadership, Higher Education, Student Services) strongly preferred.
 Experience  
 Demonstrated experience working in post-secondary student services with student, staff, and faculty. 
 Experience working with a student association/student government considered an asset.
 Program/project development and management experience is an asset.
 Demonstrated experience working with graduate students is preferred.   
 Volunteer management and student staff supervision experience – particularly in a student leadership capacity an asset.
 Knowledge/Skills/Abilities  
 A record of and commitment to participating in ongoing learning and engagement in the areas of equity, diversity, inclusion, anti-racism, and accessibility. Demonstrated experience applying this learning to their leadership and program development/design.
 Foundational understanding of the graduate student experience based on research, literature and best practice related to student retention, engagement, and development.  
 Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly, work collaboratively, build consensus and be sensitive to the needs and interests of various stakeholders, both within the department and across the institution. 
 Demonstrated ability to use and interpret data to make decisions and communicate results effectively to various stakeholders.
 Exceptional organizational skills as well as the ability to multi-task, manage, and forecast required resources. 
 Proven ability to take initiative and be both creative and flexible. 
 High degree of political acumen. 
 Demonstrated ability to contribute to and thrive in a collaborative environment and to apply a positive team approach to working with colleagues within and outside of the SSO. 
 Demonstrated ability for coaching graduate-level student staff in event management, facilitation, and program content development. 
 Equity Statement 
The University of Waterloo acknowledges that much of our work takes place on the traditional territory of the Neutral, Anishinaabeg, and Haudenosaunee peoples. Our main campus is situated on the Haldimand Tract, the land granted to the Six Nations that includes six miles on each side of the Grand River. Our active work toward reconciliation takes place across our campuses through research, learning, teaching, and community building, and is coordinated within the Office of Indigenous Relations.
The University values the diverse and intersectional identities of its students, faculty, and staff. The University regards equity and diversity as an integral part of academic excellence and is committed to accessibility for all employees. The University of Waterloo seeks applicants who embrace our values of equity, anti-racism and inclusion.  As such, we encourage applications from candidates who have been historically disadvantaged and marginalized, including applicants who identify as First Nations, Métis and/or Inuk (Inuit), Black, racialized, a person with a disability, women and/or 2SLGBTQ+.
Positions are open to qualified candidates who are legally entitled to work in Canada.
The University of Waterloo is committed to accessibility for persons with disabilities. If you have any application, interview, or workplace accommodation requests, please contact Human Resources at hrhelp@uwaterloo.ca or 519-888-4567, ext. 45935.

Huawei Canada has an immediate 8-12 month Co-op opening for an Engineer. 
 About the team: 
 Huawei Canada's Advanced Optical Technology Lab focuses on advanced R&D in high-performance optical communications and networking. Our expert team specializes in transmission algorithms, systems, physics, and AI-driven optical network management. The lab engages in projects ranging from deep research to developing key product features, actively participating in standards organizations and collaborative research with partners. Our multicultural environment fosters innovation, mentorship, and a passion for learning. If you thrive on solving complex technical challenges, this lab is your ideal place. 
 About the job: 
 Working on the next generation of short-reach and data center interconnect (DCI) networks. In this role you will focus on the design and simulation of Intensity-Modulated Direct-Detection (IMDD) transmission systems operating over cutting-edge Hollow-Core Fiber (HCF). Given the physical properties of HCF, efficient signaling and equalization methods are fundamental to achieve cost and power efficient optical links. 
 Modeling of end-to-end non-coherent optical transmission system. 
 Modeling of Hollow-Core Fiber and the impact of gas absorption on the transmission. 
 Exploring efficient signaling and equalization to combat channel induced fading profiles. 
 Studying the impact of high launch power on the system reach and performance. 
 The total target annual compensation (based on 2,080 hours per year) ranges from $58,000 to $104,000 depending on education, experience, and demonstrated expertise. 
 About the ideal candidate: 
 Currently enrolled in Master’s/PhD program in Electrical Engineering program or equivalent. 
 Solid background in non-coherent optical fiber transmission and reception. 
 Deep understanding of direct-detection systems, transceiver limitations, and noise penalties (e.g., RIN, thermal noise, shot noise). 
 Familiarity with programming languages like Matlab and/or Python. 
 Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively in a team. 
 A publication record on similar topics is an asset. 
 Applicants must be enrolled in a co-op program and be registered for an official co-op work term for the full duration of the employment period. 
 Additional Information: 
 Huawei Canada is committed to a fair, inclusive, and accessible recruitment process. If you require accommodation during any stage of the hiring process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs. 
 All applications for this position are reviewed directly by our hiring team, we do not use artificial intelligence tools to screen or select candidates.

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

About the role 

We're hiring a Chief of Staff to keep Cohere's AI organization running at full speed. You'll report to and support the Chief AI Officer and work to bridge across all teams and functions at Cohere (including research, modelling, product, delivery, security, sales and operations). In any given quarter, the org ships new AI product demos and releases, customer pilots and scaled solutions, security updates, often across regions and time zones. Your job is to make sure the right work priorities win when everything feels urgent, that our plans turn into high-quality shipped work, and that our Chief AI Officer can focus on leading instead of firefighting.

Much of this is operational: the planning calendar, the budget, the headcount plan, the weekly business reviews, the communication strategy (internal and external), the cross-functional handoffs.  Your role is the operating rhythm of the org: meetings, priorities, plans, and the decisions that come out of them.  You will be a member of an experienced, high-performing and supportive leadership team.


What you'll own 

Own the operating rhythm and planning: annual and quarterly planning, goal-setting, and the weekly and monthly business reviews. Drive budget and headcount planning against the slate, and keep both honest as priorities shift mid-quarter.

Keep major programs from colliding or stalling across research, modelling, product, delivery, and security.  Be the person teams come to when it isn't clear who owns a decision, or how to navigate trade-offs.

Be the connective tissue between the Chief AI Officer’s org and the rest of the company: cross-functional planning with product, engineering, security, and finance, so the org's commitments are realistic and its dependencies are visible.

Own and lead special projects: Lead the things that don't fit neatly on any one team's plate: a reorg, a new partnership, a flagship research event, an org-wide planning week. Own them end to end.


Who you are 

You have 12+ years of operating experience, with real time inside an AI/ML organization in a Chief of Staff, business operations, or senior program-operations seat.  You know how to partner with teams shipping fast & often to high-stakes organizations, and you know how to change course with agility when needed.

You understand how AI actually works—at the level of someone who's done it rather than managed it from a distance. You can talk credibly about how a model turns into a product, what data requirements demand from both research and engineering, and where delivery motions usually break. You're fluent in the numbers. Model performance metrics, data pipeline throughput, budget-to-impact.  You don't have to run every program yourself. You do have to understand them well enough that the people who run them respect your judgment.

You hold strategy and execution in the same hand. You can sit in a planning conversation with the Chief AI Officer in the morning and chase down a stuck deliverable in the afternoon.

You thrive in a fast-paced environment, you handle ambiguity with curiosity and confidence, you stay calm when it's messy.  You have a track record of bringing order to a fast, complex org without grinding it to a halt.

You are an outstanding communicator and know how to wield soft power. Clear writing, straight talk, the ability to influence teams and individuals, and the executive presence to represent the Chief AI Officer in high-stakes conversations.

Clubspeed & Resova 
 Build the team. Create the playbook. Scale the customer revenue engine. 
 Clubspeed and Resova provide venue management, booking, and payments technology to experience-based businesses around the world.
 We’re entering an exciting new chapter. With new investment behind the business, we’re building the teams, systems, and operating rhythms needed to accelerate growth while delivering a consistently strong experience for our customers.
 We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Sales & Customer Success to lead that transformation across our customer segments.
 The Opportunity
 This is not a role where you inherit a fully built sales and customer success machine.
 You’ll have the opportunity to help build it.
 You’ll lead and develop a growing team responsible for customer retention, expansion, and new revenue while creating the processes, playbooks, metrics, and management structure required to operate effectively at scale.
 The role requires someone who can move comfortably between strategy and execution. One day you may be designing the customer segmentation model or renewal process; the next, you may be coaching a rep through an expansion opportunity, reviewing an at-risk account, or helping close a deal.
 You’ll have meaningful ownership over how we serve and grow our SMB and Mid-Market customers—and the opportunity to build a function that can scale with the business.
 What Success Looks Like
 In this role, you will:
 Build a high-performing SMB and Mid-Market Sales & Customer Success organization with clear roles, expectations, KPIs, and accountability.
 Recruit, onboard, coach, and develop a strong team of Account Managers and Customer Success professionals.
 Create scalable customer journeys and playbooks across onboarding, adoption, retention, renewal, and expansion.
 Improve Net Revenue Retention by reducing preventable churn and creating a consistent expansion motion across the customer base.
 Establish clear forecasting and pipeline management for renewals, upsells, cross-sells, and other customer revenue opportunities.
 Introduce a scalable operating model that balances high-touch engagement for strategic customers with efficient 1-to-many programs for SMB customers.
 Build better visibility into customer health, revenue risk, and expansion potential.
 Create a disciplined, accountable culture where the team understands what great performance looks like and has the coaching and tools to achieve it.
 What You’ll Do
 Key Responsibilities
 Lead, Build & Develop the Team 
 Lead the SMB and Mid-Market Sales & Customer Success teams, establishing clear expectations, responsibilities, and performance standards.
 Own recruiting and hiring as the organization grows.
 Build structured onboarding and enablement programs that help new team members ramp quickly.
 Conduct regular 1:1s, pipeline reviews, account reviews, and call coaching.
 Develop the team’s capabilities in consultative selling, negotiation, customer relationship management, retention, and expansion.
 Establish clear individual and team KPIs and create a strong culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
 Identify performance gaps early and coach team members toward stronger outcomes.
 Build the Customer Success Operating Model 
 Design and document scalable playbooks for onboarding, adoption, account management, renewal, expansion, and churn prevention.
 Develop differentiated engagement models for SMB and Mid-Market customers based on customer value, complexity, opportunity, and risk.
 Build repeatable 1-to-many programs that allow the team to effectively support a high-volume customer base.
 Establish customer health scoring and early-warning indicators for churn and expansion opportunities.
 Define clear escalation paths and operating processes across Sales, Customer Success, Support, Implementation, Product, and Payments.
 Continuously identify opportunities to simplify workflows and improve team productivity.
 Drive Retention & Expansion 
 Own the team’s performance against Net Revenue Retention, renewal, churn, and expansion targets.
 Establish a consistent renewal process that creates visibility well in advance of contract expiration.
 Build and standardize upsell and cross-sell motions across the customer base.
 Coach the team on identifying customer needs, creating value-based expansion opportunities, and successfully navigating commercial conversations.
 Partner with internal teams to address customer risks before they become churn events.
 Step into strategic or complex customer conversations when leadership involvement can materially improve the outcome.
 Create Revenue Visibility & Accountability 
 Build accurate weekly, monthly, and quarterly forecasting for renewals, expansion, and customer revenue.
 Establish pipeline standards and operating rhythms that give leadership a clear view of expected performance.
 Track and analyze performance metrics across the customer lifecycle.
 Use product usage, customer engagement, commercial, and CRM data to identify risks and opportunities.
 Ensure CRM and Customer Success systems accurately reflect account activity, pipeline, customer health, and next steps.
 Provide leadership with clear insights into performance, trends, risks, and opportunities.
 You’ll Thrive Here If...
 You enjoy building structure where it doesn’t yet exist.
 You believe strong leadership means both setting a clear standard and actively coaching people toward it.
 You like working close to customers and are comfortable getting involved when an important account or opportunity needs help.
 You are commercially minded and view Customer Success as an important driver of revenue, not simply a support function.
 You are comfortable being accountable to clear metrics and expect the same from your team.
 You can identify what needs to be standardized without adding unnecessary process.
 You enjoy working in an environment where the business is evolving quickly and you can directly influence how the function develops.
 You are excited by the opportunity to build something that is expected to become significantly larger over time.
 Why Join Clubspeed?
 This is an opportunity to join a category-leading business at an important stage of its growth.
 We have an established customer base, proven products, and significant industry expertise—and we’re investing in building a stronger, more scalable commercial organization around them.
 You’ll have the opportunity to:
 Build and shape a critical customer-facing function.
 Hire and develop your own team.
 Influence how we segment, serve, retain, and grow our customers.
 Work directly with company leadership on revenue strategy and execution.
 Create systems and playbooks that become the foundation for future scale.
 Have a measurable impact on customer retention, expansion, and company growth.
 What You’ll Get
 Significant ownership and autonomy over the SMB and Mid-Market Sales & Customer Success organization.
 The opportunity to build rather than simply maintain an existing function.
 A seat at the table and meaningful influence over company strategy.
 A growing organization where strong performers can expand their scope as the business scales.
 The ability to make a visible impact on customers, employees, and company performance.
 Our Hiring Process
 Our hiring process is designed to be straightforward and conversational.
 We want to understand how you think, how you lead, what you’ve built before, and how you would approach scaling a customer-facing revenue organization.
 You’ll also have the opportunity to meet members of the leadership team, learn more about where Clubspeed and Resova are headed, and determine whether this is the right environment for you.
 Join Us
 If you’re excited by the opportunity to build a team, create scalable commercial processes, develop great people, and directly influence retention and growth , we’d love to hear from you.
 What We’re Looking For
 5+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, Sales, or a related commercial function.
 2+ years of direct people management or team leadership experience. 
 Demonstrated success hiring, onboarding, coaching, and developing customer-facing teams.
 Experience operating in a high-volume SMB and/or Mid-Market environment.
 Strong commercial instincts with experience managing renewals, expansion opportunities, contract negotiations, and revenue targets.
 Proven ability to build processes, playbooks, operating cadences, or functions rather than simply working within established ones.
 Strong understanding of Customer Success metrics including Net Revenue Retention, Gross Revenue Retention, churn, expansion, renewal rates, and customer health.
 Strong forecasting, pipeline management, and performance management capabilities.
 Experience using CRM and Customer Success platforms to improve visibility, automation, and team effectiveness.
 Comfort working with data and translating performance metrics into concrete actions.
 Ability to move between strategic planning and hands-on execution.
 Competitive base+bonus compensation structure
 Comprehensive health coverage, including dental and vision
 Flexible time off policy
